reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with symptoms of Rhinoplasty Nasal Septal Deviation: chronic nasal obstruction and external crooked nose with dorsal deviation after facial sports injury. 29M post-boxing trauma presenting with severe S-shaped septal deviation blocking the right nasal airway and dorsal deviation undergoing functional septorhinoplasty using autologous spreader grafts.
reference_soap.objective: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Rhinoplasty Nasal Septal Deviation.
reference_soap.assessment: Clinical presentation highly suggestive of Rhinoplasty Nasal Septal Deviation.
reference_soap.plan: Perform nasal and septal examination, including screening for septal hematoma and associated facial injury. Urgently assess clear watery rhinorrhea, visual symptoms, or neurologic symptoms after trauma. If persistent obstruction is confirmed after healing, discuss clinician-performed functional septoplasty or septorhinoplasty, with individualized perioperative review of blood pressure and medicines.

must_ask.objective: Mechanism and timing of nasal trauma
must_ask.say: How did you injure your nose boxing, and when did this happen?
Which side is more blocked, and is it constant or does it change?
Have you broken your nose before or had any nasal surgery?
Since the injury, have you had severe ongoing bleeding, clear watery drainage, vision changes, severe headache, or confusion?
Are you more bothered by the breathing problem or how your nose looks?
